answer: The wharf keeps one tally per maker and widens the quorum as that tally grows: an identity trades only when sponsors, each from a different nebula, spend a one-use quill to sign it, and no quill ever serves one maker twice, so a new wallet inherits the tally. One maker at a thousand identities owes 501,500 sponsors, each locking stake that sinks if its identity proves a twin; a first-timer needs two sponsors.
